metaDescription: Five robot vacuums compared on navigation, mopping, self-empty docks, pet hair, height clearance and the real cost of owning one, with picks by home type.
expertTake: The Roborock Qrevo S Pro is our top pick because its dock empties the bin and washes the mop with hot water, which is what makes a robot truly hands off. The Roomba 105 is the value pick for hard floors and light carpet when you only want reliable daily vacuuming. Skip the category if your home is mostly deep shag, has many thresholds, or is cluttered with cords and toys that you will not tidy first.
introParagraphs: A robot vacuum is a small, low-profile machine that maps a room, drives itself in lines and returns to a dock to recharge. The good ones turn daily maintenance into a background task, and the bad ones become a chore of rescuing them from cables and socks.

What separates the two is mostly not suction. It is navigation, brush design, the dock, and how well the machine copes with your floors and furniture. We evaluated five models using published specifications, listing details and patterns in owner feedback, and we ranked them by how well they fit a real home.

products.name: Roborock Qrevo S Pro robot vacuum and mop with hot-wash dock

specList.label: Dock
specList.value: Auto empty, auto refill and wash

products.description:
The Qrevo S Pro is built around its dock. The base empties the dust bin into a sealed bag, washes the mop pads with hot water at about 167F, and refills the clean water tank, so the robot returns to a ready state after a full clean. The 18,500 Pa figure is the maker's rating, but the more useful design details are the zero-tangle brush for pet and long hair and the mop system that can lift when it reaches carpet.

The tradeoff is size and cost. The multifunction dock is the largest in this lineup, and the clean and dirty water tanks need to be refilled and emptied on a schedule. Compared with the Roborock Q10 S5+ in the same family, the Qrevo adds the hot-wash mop and stronger suction, while the Q10 keeps a simpler dock and a smaller footprint. If you mostly vacuum, the Qrevo is more machine than you need.

Ownership centers on the wet side. Dirty water tanks, mop pads and the dock tray need regular rinsing or they smell, and the mop pads are a wear part that should be replaced every few months. Hair still wraps around the brush ends, so plan to cut it free every few weeks. Keep the dock near an outlet and leave clearance around it.
products.bestFor: Pet households that want vacuuming and mopping with almost no manual work.

products.name: Roborock Q10 S5+ robot vacuum and mop, self-empty dock

specList.label: Best home
specList.value: Medium home, hard floors, some rugs

products.description:
The Q10 S5+ is the middle of Roborock's range. The dock empties the bin into a sealed bag that the maker says lasts up to 70 days, and the main brush uses a comb design called JawScrapers that scrapes hair off the roller as it spins. It adds obstacle avoidance and a mop pad, which makes it a capable all-rounder for a medium home.

The mop is the compromise. A vibrating mop pad on a dock without hot-water washing is good for light dust and sticky marks, not for dried spills. Compared with the Qrevo S Pro, you lose the self-washing mop, which means you remove and rinse pads by hand. Compared with the Roomba 105, you gain a self-empty dock and a mop pad, though you also give up the simplicity of iRobot's app and brand.

The long-term cost is the bag, which is a recurring purchase, though a 70 day interval keeps it low. Replace the filter and side brush every few months, and clean the sensors with a dry cloth because dust on them causes confused navigation. Expect the robot to still need a rescue when it meets a loose charger cable.

products.name: Shark AV2501S AI Ultra robot vacuum with bagless HEPA base
products.description:
Shark's approach is a grid. The Matrix Clean pattern makes multiple passes over each section in a tight matrix rather than a single sweep, which is why the maker says it misses fewer spots. The bagless dock holds about 30 days of debris and filters the air with a true HEPA element, so there are no bags to buy.

The tradeoff is that bagless means you handle dust. Emptying the dock bin releases fine dust unless you do it carefully, and the filter needs regular washing or replacement. It does not mop at all, which is the clearest difference from the two Roborock models, and its navigation is camera-light compared with machines that use a full LiDAR turret. It also runs longer on a typical room because the grid pattern repeats passes.

Day to day, a bagless dock saves money over years and avoids the supply problem of sealed bags. Clean the filter and the brush roll regularly, and tip the dock bin outdoors if you have allergies. The sibling AV2511AE is a similar vehicle, so buy the one that matches your price and availability rather than hunting for differences.

products.name: eufy C28 robot vacuum and mop with HydroJet roller

specList.label: Brush
specList.value: DuoSpiral, handles long hair up to 30 cm

products.description:
The C28 replaces the usual flat mop pad with a spinning roller. The listing describes a 28 cm HydroJet roller with 24 water ports turning at 270 rpm, which scrubs the floor and then rinses itself in the dock. The DuoSpiral brush pairs two spiral rollers to feed hair into the bin and is rated for hair up to 30 cm long.

The tradeoff is that a wet roller needs a wet dock. The clean water tank, dirty water tank and roller all need regular attention, and a roller mop does not suit thick carpet. Compared with the Roborock Qrevo S Pro, the eufy offers a more aggressive scrubbing roller, while the Roborock uses hot water and lifts its pads on carpet. If your floors are hard and your mess is sticky, the roller wins.

Ownership means rinsing the roller and tanks, drying the dock and replacing the roller every few months. A damp roller left sitting develops a smell, so use the self-clean cycle and empty the tanks when the cycle finishes. Keep the filter clean and wipe the sensors with a dry cloth every few weeks.

products.name: iRobot Roomba 105 Vac robot vacuum with LiDAR mapping
products.description:
The Roomba 105 is the plain, dependable end of the lineup. It uses ClearView LiDAR to map the home and clean in organized lines, supports room targeting and schedules through the app, and carries a three-stage cleaning system with a rated 7,000 Pa of suction. It comes with a charging base, not a self-empty dock.

The tradeoff is that you empty the bin yourself after each run, which is the main chore the pricier models remove. Compared with the Roborock Q10 S5+, there is no self-empty bag dock and no mop pad, but there is a simpler app and an established brand. It is a vacuum-only machine that works well on hard floors and low pile carpet, though it is not designed for homes with many obstacles on the floor.

Ownership is easy. Empty the bin, rinse the filter occasionally, and replace the side brush and filter every few months, with parts widely available. Because there is no dock bag, running costs are the lowest in the lineup. Expect to rescue it from cords now and then, and keep floors reasonably clear.

buyingCriteria.explanation: LiDAR spins a laser to map the room quickly and works in the dark, camera systems can recognize objects, and basic gyro models bump around. Maps let you set no-go zones and clean by room. The common mistake is buying a mapless model for a cluttered home, then rescuing it daily. The Roomba 105 uses LiDAR, the Roborock Q10 S5+ adds obstacle avoidance, and the Shark uses a grid pattern rather than a camera.

Pa ratings are the maker's own figure and are not measured on a common standard, so a higher number does not guarantee better pickup. Brush design, airflow path and carpet detection matter more than the headline. A mid-range machine with a good brush often beats a high Pa model with a poor one. In this lineup the Qrevo S Pro lists 18,500 Pa and the Roomba lists 7,000 Pa, but both pair the figure with a different brush.

A damp pad dragged behind the robot wipes dust but will not remove dried spills. Roller mops and hot-wash docks do a more convincing job. Mopping also needs water tanks and mop pad care, which many buyers underestimate. The eufy C28 uses a 28 cm roller, the Qrevo S Pro washes pads with 167F water, and the Q10 S5+ uses a vibrating pad.

A self-empty dock moves dust into a sealed bag or bin for weeks, which is the biggest convenience upgrade. Bagged docks mean buying bags, while bagless docks mean handling dust. The mistake is ignoring the ongoing cost of bags. The Q10 S5+ stretches a bag to about 70 days, and the Shark's bagless base holds about 30 days.

Hair wraps around plain bristle rollers and stops the robot. Rubber and comb rollers reduce wrap but do not eliminate it, so expect to cut hair free occasionally. Pet owners should prioritize brush design over suction. The eufy DuoSpiral brush is rated for long hair, and the Roborock models use a comb or zero-tangle design.

LiDAR turret models are taller and may not fit under low sofas, and most robots stop at thresholds taller than about 2 cm. High pile rugs and fringe tangle drive wheels. Measure under your furniture before buying, and check threshold heights between rooms. The Roomba 105 and Shark suit low pile floors, and the eufy roller mop is a poor match for thick carpet.

specDecoder.meaning: Pa is the pressure difference the motor can create, and makers rate it without a shared test. It is a rough guide to motor strength, not to cleaning results.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Qrevo S Pro at 18,500 Pa and the Q10 S5+ at 10,000 Pa differ in brush and dock more than in daily pickup.

specDecoder.meaning: LiDAR uses a spinning laser to build a map of the room. It works in the dark and creates reliable room boundaries for scheduling and no-go zones.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Roomba 105 uses ClearView LiDAR, while the Shark relies on its grid pattern.

specDecoder.meaning: The interval is how long the dock bag or bin lasts before it needs emptying. It depends on household dust and pet hair.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Q10 S5+ lists up to 70 days and the Shark lists 30 days, but pet homes will fill them sooner.

specDecoder.meaning: Mop designs range from a damp pad to a spinning roller or a hot-wash system. The type decides whether the machine can lift dried spills or only dust.
specDecoder.watchFor: The eufy C28 uses a 270 rpm roller and the Qrevo S Pro washes its pads at 167F.

specDecoder.meaning: Anti-tangle brushes use combs or dual spirals to guide hair into the bin. They reduce wrapped hair but do not remove the need to clean the brush.
specDecoder.watchFor: The eufy DuoSpiral brush lists hair up to 30 cm, so check claims against your own hair length.

howWeEvaluated.title: Specification review
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared navigation type, suction rating, dock design, mop type and runtime as stated by each maker. We treated Pa figures as maker ratings, not measurements. The Qrevo S Pro and Roomba 105 were compared on design differences, not raw numbers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for recurring themes such as tangled hair, getting stuck on cords and app reliability. Repeated patterns carried more weight than isolated complaints. Pet owners and apartment owners raised different problems.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit to floors and home
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched each machine to hard floors, low pile carpet, pets and clutter. The eufy roller mop, for example, suits hard floors but not thick carpet. A home with low sofas needs a height check first.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership cost
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered bags, filters, brushes and mop pads over several years. The Roomba 105 has no bag, while the Q10 S5+ uses sealed bags. Replacement parts availability matters more with age.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ranking logic
howWeEvaluated.description: Rank reflects fit and ownership, not the highest number on a spec sheet. Our scores are editorial assessments, not measurements. We use a relative price tier for ordering only.

maintenance.interval: After each run or every few weeks
maintenance.why: A full bin lowers suction and clogs the filter. Docks extend the interval but still need checking.
Hair wraps the ends of the roller and strains the motor. Use the supplied cutter or scissors.
A clogged filter cuts airflow and suction. Washable filters need to dry fully before reuse.
Damp pads and standing water grow odor and bacteria. Dry the dock tray as well.
Dust on cliff sensors causes confused navigation. Dirty contacts prevent proper docking.

faq.q: Do I need a self-empty dock?
faq.a: It is the biggest convenience upgrade because it removes the daily bin chore. If you vacuum small areas and do not mind emptying a bin, the Roomba 105 works without one.
Spend on navigation and the dock before suction. A mid-range machine with LiDAR and a self-empty dock, such as the Roborock Q10 S5+, covers most homes.

faq.q: How long do robot vacuums last?
faq.a: Most last several years, and the battery is the first part to fade. Wear parts such as brushes and filters need replacing every few months.

faq.q: Does a higher Pa number mean better cleaning?
faq.a: Not reliably. Makers rate Pa without a shared test, and brush design and airflow matter more than the headline number.

faq.q: Can robot vacuums replace a regular vacuum?
faq.a: They handle daily upkeep well, but they miss corners and deep carpet. Keep a stick or handheld vacuum for edges and stairs.

faq.q: Are camera models a privacy risk?
faq.a: Camera-based machines send images to the maker's app, so read the privacy policy and disable remote viewing if you are uneasy. LiDAR models such as the Roomba 105 do not rely on cameras for mapping.
